text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: HIGH - kvcache eviction surge on gpu-pool-west-1 triggered (alert_id=PD-98322)

pagerduty: PagerDuty incident created: PD-98322 - kvcache_eviction_surge

jamie: saw the spike - multiple GPUs showing eviction rates > 95% and subsequent cuda alloc failures in logs

ashley: acked on PD and joining. what services impacted?

devon: looks like routed traffic to 'gen-large' model on hosted cluster - error spike on /v1/stream and token failures (rate limit?). seeing 503s and "CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY" in worker logs

leah: tagging infra for fallback. @ashley can you confirm if auto-fallback to smaller-quantized variant is enabled for that route?

ashley: auto-fallback is on for gen-large -> gen-small-q4 when latency > 800ms or OOMs detected. but the rollout may not trigger fast enough under continuous eviction.

jamie: logs snippet:```
[2026-03-14T21:05:12Z] gpu-12 kernel: cudart: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[2026-03-14T21:05:12Z] worker-gen: kv_cache_miss=0.82 kv_cache_evictions=0.97 seq_len=1024
[2026-03-14T21:05:13Z] worker-gen: falling back to cpu inference? false - dispatch failed
```

devon: customer impact: increased 5xx for hosted API keys in us-west region, but no broad outage. approx 8% of requests for gen-large returned 5xx in last 15m.

leah: status: paging second oncall and infra. plan: 1) temporarily reduce max-batch to 1 on gpu-pool-west-1 2) pin routing to gen-small-q4 for high-risk customers 3) drain nodes with highest eviction rates 4) rotate GPUs if needed

ashley: will execute batch size change now. running:```
kubectl -n inference set env ds/gen-workers MAX_BATCH=1 --selector=pool=gpu-pool-west-1
```

ashley: done, config applied.

jamie: monitoring: p99 latency dropped slightly but eviction still high on 3 nodes (gpu-12, gpu-15, gpu-20)

sre-bot: Auto-shedder triggered on pool gpu-pool-west-1, 2 workers evicted to reduce contention

devon: I'm going to drain gpu-12. command:```
kubectl -n inference cordon node gpu-12 && kubectl -n inference drain node gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

leah: good. start draining one at a time. also open a support ticket for host maintenance/firmware check if we see repeated evictions on the same host.

ashley: routed top 5 affected API keys to gen-small-q4 via routing override:```
POST /admin/routing/overrides
{"match": "model:gen-large and region:us-west", "route_to": "gen-small-q4", "ttl": 900}
```

jamie: ack. starting temporary customer-notify draft for impacted customers: short note that we saw increased errors and we're mitigating, ETA TBD.

devon: logs after drain start:```
[2026-03-14T21:12:45Z] pool-monitor: node gpu-12 cordoned
[2026-03-14T21:13:02Z] worker-gen-12: shutting down KV cache gracefully, writing 1.2GB to checkpoint
[2026-03-14T21:13:10Z] node-exporter: eviction-rate gpu-12 -> 0.65 (dropping)
```

jamie: p99 errors for gen-large down to ~2.3% from 8%. still monitoring.

leah: are any enterprise customers actively hitting SLA thresholds? ops, can we check?

ashley: pulled list - two enterprise tenants exceeded 3xx/5xx threshold (nyc-adtech and finq-core). reached out to their CSMs.

devon: suggestion: add short-term kvcache eviction tolerance flag to runtime to avoid reactive full eviction during checkpoint flush storms. but that's a code change and not for this incident. filing followup GH issue.

jamie: PD note: escalation to infra lead (oncall2) in 5m if eviction rate doesn't go below 0.3.

sre-bot: node gpu-15 reported repeated CUDA kernel timeouts; mark for reboot if eviction rate remains >0.7 after 10m

ashley: gpu-12 drain complete. kube restarted pods on healthy nodes. traffic redistributed. no further OOM logs on that node.

devon: running recovery checks: KV cache warmup on new workers showing steady hit rates now (~0.75). exception counts dropping.

jamie: update to PD: mitigation in progress, partial customer impact, fallback and draining applied, monitoring.

leah: anyone free to do an ops handoff in 20m? I need to swap to meetings.

devon: I can take the handoff. leaving notes: 1) keep an eye on eviction-rate and cuda-oom counts 2) check for repeated node reboots 3) follow up with infra if any single host shows >3 evictions in 1h 4) file postmortem with timeline and mitigation decisions

jamie: thanks devon. I'm adding runbook steps to incident ticket and linking logs.

ashley: final check: disabling auto-burst for the affected pool to avoid noisy neighbors while we stabilize. command run.

devon: leaving to monitor for 30m, will escalate to infra lead if metrics regress. handoff to devon at 2165020200.

leah: confirmed handoff. closing PD alert to oncall primary but keeping incident open for postmortem and follow-up tasks.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: PD-98322 status changed to "acknowledged" by ashley

jamie: thanks all. postmortem owner assigned: jamie. next actions: GH issue for kvcache backoff logic, infra ticket for hardware health check on gpu-15, customer comms drafted.

sre-bot: Incident metrics snapshot (15m window):
- gen-large 5xx rate: 2.1%
- kv_cache_eviction_mean: 0.38
- cuda_oom_count: 12 (down from 48)
- affected_nodes: [gpu-15, gpu-20]

devon: I'll leave a quick note in #customer-support to coordinate any follow-up comms.

jamie: thread summary: kvcache eviction storm caused transient CUDA OOMs -> applied batch size limit, routing override to smaller quantized model, drained worst nodes, disabled auto-burst; customer impact limited but two enterprise tenants notified. handoff complete.

leah: :thumbsup: great job team. will sync on postmortem tomorrow 10:00 UTC.
